clue.text: Islamic warrior makes raw food popular

parts.note: a salad is a dish of raw vegetables
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A Muslim fighter turns uncooked food into a hit.
explanation.definitionFit: Saladin was the twelfth-century Muslim sultan who fought the Crusaders.

clue.text: So, no fabulous bird coming in? That's a blow!

indicators.note: coming in tells us one word goes inside another

parts.note: sic is Latin for so or thus
the roc is a giant bird of legend
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: No mythical bird arriving? What a disappointment!
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming in' is the container signal; 'So' is Latin sic, and 'blow' looks like a setback but means a wind.
explanation.definitionFit: A sirocco is a hot wind that blows from North Africa.

clue.text: Loss in every game — that wasn't arranged

explanation.surface: Someone loses every single game, and it was not fixed.
explanation.walkthrough: In tennis, losing every game means the opponent's score stays at love, nothing; a marriage made for affection, not by parents, is the other sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A match where one side wins every game ends with the other on love, or zero; a marriage for affection rather than one planned by families.

clue.text: Do in full once more

explanation.surface: Perform it completely again.
explanation.definitionFit: 'do.' is the abbreviation for this word, meaning the same again, so written in full it is that word; repeated means again.

clue.text: Silvery element cook put in menu

indicators.note: to cook something is to falsify or rework it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A chef puts a shiny metal on the menu.
explanation.definitionFit: Neptunium is a silvery radioactive metallic element, number 93.

clue.text: Saw one demonstrating to the business beginner

parts.note: a prover is one who proves or demonstrates something

indicators.note: the beginner of a word is its opening letter, here taken from business

explanation.surface: A tool is used by someone giving a demonstration to a business novice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like the tool or a past tense; it is a noun meaning an old saying. 'to the' merely links.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying or maxim, a synonym.

clue.text: Imitation ice? Could be fishy

explanation.surface: Fake diamonds might seem suspect.
explanation.walkthrough: Ice is slang for diamonds; paste is glass used for imitation gems, and fish paste is a spread.
explanation.definitionFit: Paste is a glassy material for imitation jewels; a spread such as fish paste.

clue.text: Make king take queen, perhaps, to open Parliament once

parts.note: overt means open, not hidden
the Rump Parliament was the remnant of the English Long Parliament in the 1640s and 1650s

explanation.surface: A monarch is made to marry a queen at a past opening of Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: In card games a king and a queen are cards: to overtrump is to beat a trump already played with a higher one.
explanation.definitionFit: To overtrump is to play a higher trump card than one already played.

clue.text: Ungenerous price for rolls

explanation.surface: A stingy cost for bread rolls.
explanation.walkthrough: Even money is a mean price for a bettor; it also means flattens, as a roller does.
explanation.definitionFit: Odds of even money are a short, mean return for a gambler; to smooth out is what a roller does.

clue.text: After fight, matchmaker may be hedging

indicators.note: After places the matchmaker word behind the fight word

parts.note: to box is to fight
wood is what matches are made from

explanation.surface: After a bout, a marriage broker may be evasive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'matchmaker' suggests a marriage broker; matches are made of wood. 'hedging' looks like evasion but means forming hedges.
explanation.definitionFit: Box is a shrub widely planted to form garden hedges.

clue.text: Check on state of bolt

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing on another is placed after it

parts.note: RI is the abbreviation for Rhode Island, a US state
to vet is to check or examine

explanation.surface: Someone inspects the condition of a door bolt.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' means placed after; 'Check' looks like the definition but is the verb vet.
explanation.definitionFit: A rivet is a metal pin or fastening bolt.

clue.text: Can no two Parisians dance this? On the contrary

definitions.text: Can no two Parisians dance this? On the contrary

parts.words: Can no two Parisians dance this? On the contrary
parts.note: the French name of this ballet dance reads literally as 'not of two', yet it is a dance for exactly two people, Parisians or not

explanation.surface: A question whether no pair of Parisians can perform a dance, answered in the negative.
explanation.walkthrough: French 'pas' means both 'step' and 'not', so the name seems to say 'no two', while the dance is in fact for a pair.
explanation.definitionFit: A pas de deux is a ballet dance for two performers.

clue.text: Mixture's put by river for coolness

parts.note: compo is a mixture such as mortar, here with its possessive s kept
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, northern England

explanation.surface: A blend is placed next to a river to keep it cool.
explanation.definitionFit: Composure is calmness, the quality of keeping cool under pressure.

clue.text: Italian poet news agency got round

parts.note: TASS was the Soviet news agency
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A news service gets around to covering an Italian poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Torquato Tasso was a sixteenth-century Italian epic poet.

clue.text: Poor shot dismissed by king

parts.note: a batsman dismissed in cricket is out
ER, Edward Rex, stands for a king

explanation.surface: A bad stroke gets a player sent off by the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: In archery or shooting an outer is a hit in the outermost ring of the target, a weak shot.

clue.text: Old relative is breaking journey to the Mexican border

indicators.note: is breaking says one word is split open by the other

parts.note: a ride is a journey
gran is a grandmother

explanation.surface: An elderly relative is interrupting a trip to Mexico's border.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rio Grande river forms much of the frontier between the USA and Mexico.

clue.text: Silly, but such a person may be appealing

definitions.text: such a person may be appealing

explanation.surface: A foolish person might nonetheless be attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appealing' looks like charming; in the second reading it means lodging an appeal, as someone who feels wrongly judged does.
explanation.definitionFit: Silly means unwise or poorly thought out; someone appealing against a verdict claims to have been wrongly assessed in court.

clue.text: Feature of the English — the last word in dressing

indicators.note: in tells us the first pieces sit inside the dressing word

parts.note: lint is a fabric used for dressing wounds
amen is said at the end of a prayer, the last word

explanation.surface: The English trait of having the final say on how to dress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dressing' looks like clothing or salad dressing; it is a wound dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: Lineaments are the distinctive features of a face.

clue.text: Plain cage, perhaps, but it has snazzy bars

indicators.note: perhaps suggests these letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A plain cage may still have flashy bars.
explanation.definitionFit: A gin palace was a showy Victorian pub, and its bars are places serving drink.

clue.text: Old Pauline theologians?

parts.note: Old Paulines are former pupils of St Paul's School in London, so they are men of a school; the real sense is medieval university theologians

explanation.walkthrough: An Old Pauline is an old boy of St Paul's School, London, which makes the theologians seem to be followers of St Paul.
explanation.definitionFit: The medieval scholastic philosophers and theologians of the universities are called by this name.

clue.text: One deeply dangerous was about to seek a compliment

parts.note: saw about, or saw to, means attended to
to fish for compliments is to seek praise

explanation.surface: A dangerous person was on the verge of fishing for praise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deeply' means in the deep sea; the toothed snout makes the creature dangerous.
explanation.definitionFit: The sawfish is a large ray with a toothed snout living in the sea.

clue.text: Pimp heard police car

indicators.note: heard means the word is spoken, and its sound gives the answer

parts.note: to pander is to act as a pimp, and a pander is a pimp

explanation.surface: A procurer listens to a squad car.
explanation.walkthrough: A panda car is a British term for a small police patrol car, once painted in black and white.
explanation.definitionFit: A panda car is a British patrol vehicle used by the police.

clue.text: Request to lead off the ball — sideways

parts.note: to ask is to request

indicators.note: lead off says the leading letter of the word for ball is removed

parts.note: a ball is a dance

explanation.surface: An invitation to open the dancing, given with a sidelong glance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead off' suggests opening the dance; it removes D from DANCE, leaving ANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: To look askance is to glance sideways, often with suspicion.

clue.text: Ladies' group back theatre cleaner

parts.note: the WI, Women's Institute, is a British women's organisation

indicators.note: back tells us the word for theatre is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: rep is repertory theatre

explanation.surface: A women's club supports a theatre's cleaning lady.
explanation.definitionFit: A wiper is something that cleans, such as a windscreen wiper.

clue.text: One of baby's things was cracked

explanation.surface: One of the baby's things was broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracked' looks like broken; here it means crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: A toddler's chamber pot; British slang for crazy.

clue.text: Wodehouse's old characters discuss Jack's growth

parts.note: P. G. Wodehouse's characters greet each other as 'old bean'
to talk is to discuss

explanation.surface: Wodehouse's characters chat about how Jack has grown up.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack is the boy in the fairy tale 'Jack and the ...', whose magic plant grows to the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: In the fairy tale Jack climbs a giant plant grown from magic beans.

clue.text: Cupid's pub-crawl

explanation.surface: The god of love goes on a drinking tour.
explanation.walkthrough: Cupid is traditionally shown with a blindfold; a drinking spree is also called by this word in British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Love is said to be without sight, like Cupid; a bout of heavy drinking.

clue.text: Star's room upstairs

explanation.surface: A celebrity's attic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star' looks like a celebrity; the sun is our star.
explanation.definitionFit: Of the sun, the nearest star; an upper living room in a medieval house.

clue.text: Decimal point entered by one very thorough

indicators.note: entered by tells us the first pieces are broken into by the following ones

parts.note: decimal counting is done in tens
E, east, is a compass point
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A decimal point is typed in by someone extremely meticulous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entered by' puts IV inside INTENSE (IN TENS plus E); 'Decimal point' looks like one unit but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Intensive work is concentrated and thorough.

clue.text: Experience in field service

parts.note: lea is a poetic word for a meadow or field
RN, the Royal Navy, is one of the armed services

explanation.surface: Someone has experience working in a field service.
explanation.definitionFit: To learn of something is to come to know it, as through experience.

clue.text: American rustic dance origin

parts.note: a hay is an old country dance
a seed is the origin of something

explanation.surface: A rural dance from America is traced to its roots.
explanation.definitionFit: A hayseed is US slang for a country bumpkin.

clue.text: Earthen dish, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the word is said out loud and its sound gives the answer

parts.note: a tureen is a deep serving dish for soup

explanation.surface: A clay dish is reported.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrene means of the earth, earthy or earthly.
